speaker: Warren Ashford
cascadeSummary: In Cycle 106, I advanced the Temescal Community Health Center into utility inspections while tying construction milestones to ongoing fiscal audit checkpoints. For Rockridge, I requested a targeted commercial corridor assessment from Economic Development rather than approving blank-check programs. Across KONO and Temescal, I defended District 7 by demanding transparent service-gap accounting and taking credit for the disciplined execution keeping Temescal projects on schedule.

statements.topic: Temescal Community Health Center Construction Milestone
statements.decision: Authorize progression to interior wall framing and utility inspections subject to budget audit verification
statements.quote: The frame is up because District 7 demanded strict timelines, and we will keep the ledger balanced as utility inspections begin.
statements.fullStatement: The structural frame of the Temescal Community Health Center stands ahead of schedule because we treated the $45 million budget with rigorous oversight rather than casual rhetoric. Moving into interior framing and utility inspections this cycle is the direct result of operational discipline on the ground. I support advancing to this phase, but City Hall must remember that speed cannot outpace fiscal accountability. We will inspect every conduit and audit every dollar before final disbursement.

statements.decision: Direct Economic Development to conduct a targeted merchant retention audit for Rockridge
statements.quote: We do not solve quiet storefronts in Rockridge by throwing money into the dark—we demand data on merchant retention first.
statements.fullStatement: Rockridge is experiencing subtle commercial friction and shifting daily activity, yet City Hall's default response is either total neglect or unmetered spending. I am directing the Economic Development Department to deliver a comprehensive merchant retention audit and retail vacancy report for College Avenue. District 7 requires targeted, data-backed stabilization that protects existing local businesses rather than broad municipal subsidies that lack performance metrics.

statements.topic: District 7 Economic Oversight and Service Allocation
statements.decision: Order service gap reports for KONO and formally claim credit for Temescal capital project execution
statements.quote: Temescal is thriving because of District 7 discipline, and KONO will get targeted support only when the service gap audit is on my desk.
statements.fullStatement: While others rush to claim credit for Temescal's upbeat momentum and bustling street activity, that success was built on District 7 holding contractors and city departments to strict performance benchmarks. In KONO, steady commercial activity does not excuse City Hall from delivering basic municipal services. I will not endorse blanket funding without the pending Economic Development service gap analysis in hand. We govern District 7 by the numbers, not by guesswork.
